Subject: Sudden throughput drop + 5xx after v3-qprofile deploy

Hi Kimberly,

We started seeing a major throughput collapse and spike in 5xx errors about 45 minutes after we took the v3-qprofile+quant build live (v3.0.2). P95 latency is also up ~3x for our hotpath. This is impacting checkout flows for a subset of customers.

We rolled traffic back on our side but the traffic patterns still show instability — some requests return 500s, others time out. Attached are a couple of snapshots and our logs from the last hour.

Can Redwood confirm whether any runtime changes or kernel updates were rolled alongside this profile? We need an ETA for either a mitigation plan or rollback assist. Our CTO (Michael) is on standby.

Thanks,
Elena Ruiz
Ops Lead, Storvia

On Fri, Oct 9, 2026 at 6:25 PM Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.com> wrote:
> Aditya (Eng) — I’m asking our infra team to look for any correlation with the qprofile flip and kernel selection.

Preliminary notes from infra: the v3-qprofile includes an updated decode kernel that changes attention tile sizes and a different KV cache packing layout. In our canaries we didn’t hit this path for sequences longer than 512 tokens. Storvia’s hotpath predominantly uses 1024 tokens and the traffic spike appears to trigger a decoder fallback path that introduces contention on the KV cache lock. That would explain intermittent 500s (resource exhaustion) + p95 latency blowups.

What we need from Storvia ASAP: the full perf_logs_1010.zip (kernel traces, per-request KV cache metrics) and the trace_id list for several 500s so we can map to specific kernel frames. If you’re open to it, we can attempt a live toggle to the v2-stable qprofile on a small percentage of traffic first (canary rollback) to validate.

Tentative mitigation options (short term):
- Canary rollback to v2-stable (recommended immediate).
- Reduce batch_size and cap max_seq_len to 512 for affected routes as a temporary throttle.
- Recompile affected kernel path to use conservative tile sizes (more work).

I’ll keep digging; flagging to Markus since this is likely to need exec attention if it’s impacting checkout.

—Aditya
Staff Software Engineer, Inference Runtime
From: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.com>
To: kimberly_park@redwood.com, ben_carter@redwood.com, aditya_rao@redwood.com, marissa_cole@redwood.com
Date: Sat, 10 Oct 2026 01:05:00 -0700
Subject: Exec visibility: Storvia throughput/5xx escalation — recommendation

Team — I’ve reviewed Aditya’s notes. This is a high-impact production regression on an upgrade path that changed decode kernel behavior. Next steps I’m asking for immediately:
1) If Storvia approves, we perform an assisted canary rollback to v2-stable across 10% of their traffic within the hour. If metrics improve, expand to 100% and declare mitigation.
2) Open a postmortem priority ticket (SUP-1234) and assign runtime + compiler leads.
3) Notify C-suite at Storvia (Michael Song) and offer an exec sync in the next 2 hours.

We should avoid a code-level patch in prod without a rollback; the conservative path is rollback + root-cause. Ben — please coordinate the communication and make sure we have the MAM signed if Storvia wants Redwood to act on their behalf. Marissa — stand up the bridge and collect the extra traces.

Markus Klein
VP, Engineering
